sections.title: Introduire le vaccin contre l’hépatite B dans les services nationaux de vaccination
Vaccination contre l’hépatite B

summary.text: Opens a French WHO fact sheet on hepatitis B vaccination by describing hepatitis B as a major global public health problem, with about 2 billion people infected and 350 million chronically infected. It notes that a safe, effective vaccine has existed for over 20 years and could prevent most hepatitis B deaths, and that preventing chronic infection also reduces onward transmission.

sections.extract: Généralités L’hépatite B (HépB) est un problème de santé publique majeur dans le monde. Environ 30 % de la population mondiale est séropositive pour le virus de l’hépatite B (HBV), soit 2 milliards d’individus infectés par le HBV. summary.text: Sets out hepatitis B vaccination strategies in French, giving priority to routine infant vaccination and adding a birth dose where perinatal transmission is common, as in South-East Asia. It explains when catch-up vaccination of older groups makes sense and how monovalent and combined vaccines should be used. It describes three schedule options linked to DTP visits, weighing cost against ease of delivery. It closes with advice on using vaccine introduction to strengthen immunisation services and on budgeting for start-up and recurrent costs; the extracted text contains repeated words and rows of layout symbols.

sections.extract: 1211 Genève 27 2002 Stratégies vaccinales Vaccination systématique du nourrisson. La vaccination de tous les nourrissons contre l’hépatite B, en tant que partie intégrante dans les calendriers nationaux de vaccination infantile est une priorité dans tous les pays.
